topic: Soil Organic Carbon and Microbial Dynamics in Semi-Arid Drylands
scientific_summary: In semi-arid and arid agricultural zones, soil organic carbon (SOC) below 0.6% indicates severe biological exhaustion, resulting in collapsed aggregate stability, elevated bulk density (>1.45 g/cm³), and compromised mycorrhizal colonization. Increasing SOC by 0.2-0.4% per hectare improves soil available water capacity (AWC) by 1.5-2.2% volumetric water content.

interventions.name: Legume-Based Cover Cropping & Green Manuring
interventions.mechanism: Biological nitrogen fixation via Rhizobium symbiosis coupled with root exudate allocation promotes glomalin production and microbial aggregation.

quantitative_impact.water_retention_increase_mm_m: 12 - 18 mm per meter of soil profile

citations: FAO (2021). Recarbonizing Global Soils: A Technical Manual of Recommended Management Practices. Vol 3: Cropland, Grassland, Integrated Systems. Rome.
Lal, R. (2020). Soil organic matter content and crop yield. Journal of Soil and Water Conservation, 75(2), 27A-32A.

interventions.name: Biochar and Compost Co-Application
interventions.mechanism: Pyrolyzed biomass creates recalcitrant carbon scaffolds with high specific surface area (>250 m²/g), increasing cation exchange capacity (CEC) and protecting labile organic matter from mineralization.
citations: Lehmann, J., & Joseph, S. (2015). Biochar for Environmental Management: Science, Technology and Implementation. Routledge.
IPCC (2019). Climate Change and Land: Special Report on climate change, desertification, land degradation, sustainable land management. Ch. 4.

topic: Soil Acidity, Salinity, and Microbial Respiration
scientific_summary: Soil pH deviations outside 6.0-7.5 drastically suppress bacterial nitrogenase activity and phosphate solubilization. High electrical conductivity (>4 dS/m) induces osmotic shock in soil microarthropods and earthworms, dropping epigeic faunal diversity by over 60%.

interventions.name: Halophytic and Deep-Rooting Perennial Forage Integration
interventions.mechanism: Phytoremediation using salt-accumulating chenopods and deep-rooted grasses lowers water tables, prevents capillary rise of saline groundwater, and deposits organic acids that lower rhizosphere alkalinity.
citations: Qadir, M., et al. (2014). Economics of salt-induced land degradation and restoration. Natural Resources Forum, 38(4), 282-295.
FAO (2022). Global Status of Salt-Affected Soils. Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations.
